author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Volunteers with the Manville Share Shack are collecting and sorting back-to-school clothing for Rhode Island children whose families need help starting the academic year.

Founders Annette and Tom Briand organized the effort with Pretty Cares Inc., a Woonsocket nonprofit. The Enrico Caruso Club in Lincoln donated space on Labor Day so volunteers could bring the collection together, assess donations and prepare items for distribution.

The organizers used social media to connect with both donors and families. The request focused on practical school clothing, turning individual contributions into a coordinated community supply rather than a conventional resale operation.

The clothing is expected to be distributed at a free community event next weekend. Organizers had not published a final count of donated items or participating families in the source report, but the sorting effort was already underway. The drive extends the Share Shack’s neighborhood model: residents leave usable goods and others take what they need, with no charge and a focus on keeping support local.
dek: The Manville Share Shack and Pretty Cares are sorting donated clothing for a free community distribution planned for next weekend.
headline: Manville volunteers prepare back-to-school clothes for local children
